Encouraging to see focus on women’s health, but let’s not ignore the root issue: NIH’s history of funneling billions into bureaucratic bloat while rural clinics struggle. The Biden-era HRSA dumped $15M into “maternal health networks” last year—yet maternal mortality rates keep climbing. RFK Jr. was right to challenge NIH’s stranglehold on research funding.

Real progress means cutting red tape, not writing bigger checks to the same failed systems. Prioritize transparency, slash admin waste, and put patients before paperwork.

The House’s $452 billion VA allocation sounds massive—until you realize the VA’s budget ballooned 63% since 2019 with homelessness still surging. Throwing cash at bureaucracy isn’t “putting America first.” The Military Construction, Veterans Affairs Appropriations Act (H.R. 4366) includes $3.1B for veteran homelessness, but the VA’s own audits show 33% of homeless program funds get lost in administrative bloat.

Meanwhile, the Pakistan Democracy Act (H.R. 2311) still siphons millions abroad while vets sleep on streets.

Audit every dollar. Redirect foreign aid waste to VA caseworkers who actually fix problems.

Letlow’s district tour highlights what Washington ignores: real infrastructure needs vs. endless foreign aid handouts. Until we slash the $47B in annual hospital admin waste and redirect funds from globalist pet projects, these facilities will keep struggling.

Efficiency isn’t partisan—it’s survival.
